findings.title: Cross-squad contradiction on unpinned GitHub Actions: CICD-001 claims 29 refs in ci.yml, DEP-005 scopes same subject to ci.yml; ground truth is 18 in ci.yml, 30 across all workflows
findings.description: CICD-001 (high) titled '29 mutable-tag action references unpinned' in ci.yml with breakdown checkout@v4 x18 + dtolnay@v1 x12 (=30, internally inconsistent). DEP-005 (medium) describes the same subject scoped to ci.yml. Verified: ci.yml contains exactly 18 (checkout@v4 x11, dtolnay x7); the x18+x12 breakdown matches the ALL-workflows total of 30. CICD-001's numbers are real but misattributed to ci.yml and mislabeled 29; one report's scoping must be wrong.
findings.root_cause: Two squads enumerated the same supply-chain defect with different scopes (file vs directory) and neither cross-validated; title arithmetic was not re-checked against the breakdown.
findings.impact: Master tracker would record two overlapping tickets with contradictory counts (29 vs 18 vs 30), corrupting remediation scope estimates for the CI supply-chain fix.
findings.recommendation: Merge into ONE ticket scoped to .github/workflows/*.yml: 30 unpinned mutable-tag refs (18 checkout@v4, 12 dtolnay@v1), 18 of them in ci.yml; pin by SHA like the sibling actions already do. Canonical severity: high (CICD-001's rating stands).

fix_examples.before: Two tracker entries: 'ci.yml: 29 unpinned action refs' (high) + 'ci.yml: toolchain/checkout use mutable major-tags' (medium)
fix_examples.after: One entry: '.github/workflows: 30 unpinned mutable-tag action refs (18 in ci.yml); pin all by commit SHA'

findings.fix_guide: In every workflow step using actions/checkout@v4 or dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1, replace the major tag with the full commit SHA plus a version comment, matching the existing SHA-pinned sibling actions in the same files.

effort_estimate.breakdown: 30 SHA lookups ~20min + 30 edits ~15min + one ci.yml smoke run ~10min

detection_method.tool: audit cross-report diff + PowerShell regex count

confidence.rationale: Occurrence-level regex count run twice (line-scan 18 and occurrence-scan 18); all-workflows count 30 exactly matches CICD-001's breakdown, proving misattribution rather than fabricated numbers.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Both prior reports mechanically verified the same defect class; only count/scope adjudication is new, backed by direct file measurement.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: AGENTS.md NOTES (CI hard gates section); no ErrorCode or API-stability surface touched

findings.title: Duplicate finding with severity disagreement: OB-001 (high) vs FT-002 (medium) flag the identical runtime::init()/panic-hook unwired defect
findings.description: Observability (AUD-OB-001, high) and fault-tolerance (AUD-FT-002, medium) independently report that runtime::init() (lib.rs:141) has zero callers, leaving the T1 buff-span panic hook and .buffmap emission dead in generated programs, REPL and Jupyter. Facts agree (verified: repo-wide grep finds no caller outside buff-lang-runtime); ratings differ by one level. Also contradicts root AGENTS.md:27 which lists buff-lang-debug-info 'panic hook (T1)' as a shipped capability.
findings.root_cause: Same code-level defect is visible from two audit lenses (observability chain vs process fault-tolerance); squads did not dedupe because severity framing differed.
findings.impact: Duplicate tickets risk double-fix or contradictory triage priority (medium could be deferred while high is not), and AGENTS.md keeps advertising a runtime feature that never activates.
findings.recommendation: Track as one issue with canonical id AUD-OB-001 at high severity; fold FT-002 in. Fix: call runtime::init() from the CLI run/build entry points (and REPL/Jupyter bootstrap) so the panic hook and .buffmap emission activate.

fix_examples.before: pub fn init() { ... } // zero callers: generated programs and REPL/Jupyter lack the T1 panic hook
fix_examples.after: // crates/buff-lang-cli entry: buff_lang_runtime::init()?; before executing user code, so panics render buff-span traces and .buffmap is emitted

findings.fix_guide: Add a single init call at CLI process start (and REPL/Jupyter startup), guarded to run once; add an integration test asserting a panicking .buff program emits a buff-span trace.

effort_estimate.breakdown: wire init at 3 entry points ~40min + once-guard ~10min + integration test ~50min + snapshot update ~20min

findings.verification_command: Get-ChildItem crates -Directory | Where-Object { $_.Name -ne 'buff-lang-runtime' } | ForEach-Object { Get-ChildItem $_.FullName -Recurse -Include *.rs -File } | Select-String 'runtime::init\(\)' -List | ForEach-Object { $_.Path }

confidence.rationale: Both squads cite the same symbol and file; independent grep confirms zero external callers; AGENTS.md counter-claim located at line 27.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Verification is a direct exhaustive caller search; init() confirmed at lib.rs:141.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: AGENTS.md STRUCTURE (debug-info row); no ErrorCode changes

findings.title: Tri-squad broken-URL overlap adjudicated: PR-006 owns the buff-lang-org 404 root cause; CI-001 owns the playground relative-path root cause; AM-001/AM-002 are duplicates with a high-vs-low severity split to reconcile
findings.description: Product-roadmap (AUD-PR-006, medium), acquisition-metrics (AUD-AM-001, medium) and competitive-intel (AUD-CI-001, high) all touch broken buff URLs. Ground truth: canonical origin is vinaosb/buff (git remote -v verified); website/index.html:402 (plus benchmarks.html and playground/index.html) link to nonexistent github.com/buff-lang/buff (AM-001 duplicates PR-006's root cause). Separately, all website playground CTAs use ./playground/index.html which resolves to nonexistent website/playground/ (CI-001 verified; AM-002 reports the sibling ../playground divergence in benchmarks.html - same mechanism, rated low vs CI-001's high).
findings.root_cause: One deployment/branding root cause (wrong org) and one packaging root cause (relative-path base) each surfaced to three squads through different surfaces (README vs website vs book/marketing lens).
findings.impact: Three tickets for two defects fragments the fix; the low rating on AM-002 would bury the benchmarks-page funnel break that is high-impact in deployment.
findings.recommendation: Assign ownership: PR-006 canonical for the org-404 fix across README+website+playground (keep AM-001 as duplicate); CI-001 canonical for the relative-path fix (keep AM-002 as duplicate, adopt high severity). Replace ./playground/ with a configurable site-root-relative base and point all GitHub links at vinaosb/buff.
findings.fix_guide: Sweep website/, playground/, README.md and installers for buff-lang org references and for ./playground vs ../playground divergence; add a link-check CI step (pages deploy preview) so regressions gate.
findings.technology: Static site, GitHub Pages, marketing funnel

detection_method.tool: cross-squad diff + href grep + git remote

confidence.rationale: Canonical remote verified via git; footer buff-lang/buff link and ./playground CTAs verified at exact lines; playground is a sibling of website/ (no nested dir).

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: All three squads mechanically verified the 404s (AM-001 via live fetch); adjudication only reassigns ownership/severity, no new factual claim.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: AGENTS.md website/playground entries; PT-BR naming convention untouched

findings.title: Systemic knowledge-base staleness pattern: 14 findings from 9 squads all trace to unrefreshed AGENTS.md-family docs; root AGENTS.md self-contradicts at lines 3-9
findings.description: Pattern synthesis (do not action instances individually): AUD-PR-001 (root header wrong commit/branch/Next), AUD-CQ-007+AUD-AR-002 (buff-lang-cli AGENTS: '21 subcommands' vs verified 37; obsolete pipeline-layout text while lib.rs:50-54 re-exports buff_lang_pipeline exactly as root AGENTS claims), AUD-AR-004 (ARCHITECTURE.md inventory gaps), AUD-AR-005 (leaf-crate convention contradicted), AUD-DEP-006 (obsolete dioxus drift warning), AUD-DEP-007 (version-tier claim wrong and self-contradictory), AUD-DEP-009 (crates-io/ described as existing but absent), AUD-RF-004 (refactoring-state stale), AUD-LMAS-002/003+AUD-PR-004 (.sisyphus AGENTS vs disk/boulder), AUD-PR-003 (deferral targets 21 minors overdue), AUD-LIC-001 (editors/vscode subtree claims), AUD-CICD-008 (ci.yml comment claims HARD GATE; AGENTS.md correctly says count-only). Direct verification: AGENTS.md line 9 says 'Next: v1.26' while lines 3-4 declare v1.39 shipped. Contrast: root-level numeric claims that CAN be checked hold ('37 subcommands' true; 62-ErrorCode story coherent across code/docs/errors(62 pages)/book-minus-ch8).
findings.root_cause: No refresh gate: KB files are hand-maintained prose and pointers, updated per-campaign but never reconciled at release cuts (v1.26-v1.39 shipped without a KB sweep).
findings.impact: Every squad loses time re-adjudicating doc-vs-code conflicts (14 findings); contributors and the launch funnel inherit wrong instructions (subcommand counts, install paths, gate semantics).
findings.recommendation: One systemic fix: (1) release-cut checklist item 'refresh AGENTS.md/ARCHITECTURE.md/README status tables'; (2) generate checkable facts (crate count, subcommand count, ErrorCode count/families, version tiers) from cargo metadata into a single included snippet; (3) CI doc-drift job failing on count mismatch.

fix_examples.before: v1.25-v1.38 shipped (...). Next: v1.26 real use cases + launch infra (see .sisyphus/plans/v1.26-real-use-cases-launch.md).
fix_examples.after: v1.25-v1.39 shipped (...). Next: v1.40 (post-v1.39 backlog; see .sisyphus/plans/ for the active plan referenced by boulder.json).

findings.fix_guide: Replace inline magic numbers in AGENTS.md with placeholders sourced from a generated FACTS.md (cargo metadata + enum counts), add a weekly/README-at-tag-time drift check to ci.yml, and backfill the v1.26 pointer per AUD-PR-001/PR-002.

effort_estimate.breakdown: FACTS.md generator ~3h + AGENTS.md rewrite ~2h + CI drift job ~1h + review ~2h

findings.title: Strategic coherence (Rumelt): stated priorities (compile-speed MOAT, self-hosting, launch readiness) do not align with defect mass - launch/marketing surfaces are broken and flagship MOAT claims are unsubstantiated while compiler internals are comparatively healthy
findings.description: Single synthesis finding: across the 101-finding set, the deepest recent investment (v1.25-v1.39: generics, self-host ports, perf, bootstrap gate) matches stated MOAT priorities and shows health (AUD-LMAS-NEG clean T-number traceability, AUD-FT-008 zero undocumented unwrap violations, verified-real 37-subcommand surface), yet 'launch readiness' is contradicted by the outermost funnel: install paths 404 (PR-006), primary conversion CTAs dead (AM-001/CI-001), README status table broken markdown (PR-005), benchmarks evidence surface internally inconsistent 7-vs-6 (CI-003), release artifacts unsigned (CICD-004). The marketed MOAT itself is overclaimed: README/website present-tense Rayon+GPU dispatch vs book admissions it is not wired end-to-end (CI-002, CI-006), T1 panic hook dead (CC-002), quality gates advisory despite 'hard gate' prose (TC-005, CICD-008). This is systematic drift: internal capability outran external truth-in-marketing and funnel hardening.
findings.root_cause: Roadmap rewarded compiler-surface milestones; no acceptance criterion ever covered 'claims substantiated' or 'funnel works end-to-end', so launch-readiness was declared without a launch-surface gate.
findings.impact: Launch narrative is falsifiable in minutes by any evaluator (click install link or playground CTA): reputational risk directly offsets the MOAT investment; internal gates (advisory tests) mean the polish that did ship cannot regress-block.
findings.recommendation: Before the next compiler wave, run one 'substantiate the storefront' iteration: fix funnel URLs/table (CC-003, PR-005), reconcile MOAT claims to the book's honest state (CI-002/CI-006 wording), wire the panic hook (CC-002), make test jobs blocking or rename the gate prose - each maps 1:1 to existing findings, no new discovery needed.

fix_examples.before: emits both a Rayon path and a WGSL shader, then the runtime picks at execution time (present tense, README:42-46)
fix_examples.after: designs both a Rayon path and a WGSL shader; end-to-end GPU dispatch is in progress - see the examples legend for what runs today

findings.fix_guide: Adopt a claims ledger: every README/website performance or capability sentence links to a runnable example or benchmark; CI pages job fails if a ledger row loses its evidence; ship the storefront fixes above as the v1.40 theme.

effort_estimate.breakdown: funnel fixes 1.5h + claims ledger authoring 4h + wording reconciliation 2h + gate flip discussion/tests 8h (excludes CC-002 wiring tracked separately)

detection_method.tool: cross-squad defect-mass mapping vs roadmap priorities

confidence.rationale: Direction is a judgment call but rests on mechanically verified inputs (404s, unwired hook, advisory jobs, healthy internals); marked medium confidence because prioritization is owner's call.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Strategic synthesis cannot be proven by a single grep; mitigated by citing only prior-squad-verified facts and repo-checkable surfaces, and capped at one finding per instructions.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: AGENTS.md OVERVIEW priorities + README roadmap tables; no ErrorCode/stability surfaces touched
